system.name: Jailbreak Foundry (JBF)
system.one_liner: Multi-agent system that turns jailbreak papers into runnable attack modules and evaluates them in one unified harness for reproducible benchmarking.

content.variant_note: three titled module containers in one row (FORGE, LIB, EVAL), fed by two inputs above and fanning out to three result boxes below, with one dashed loop at the registry
content.argues: One system covers the whole path from a new jailbreak paper to a registered runnable attack and to comparable, versioned evaluation results.
content.subject: Paper-to-attack agents, a shared contract library with a registry, and a fixed evaluation harness that outputs versioned results.

encoding.color_means: tint names the module (blue = JBF-FORGE, grey = JBF-LIB, peach = JBF-EVAL); each outgoing arrow takes its source module's colour; dark green = the two inputs; orange pills = input status
encoding.line_style_means: dashed green = optional reference-repo input; dashed grey loop = continuous ingestion / versioned release; solid = main flow
encoding.shape_means: large rounded tinted container = system component; white rounded card = sub-module or output; offset stack of four cards = registry of many attack modules; pill = status tag or activity label
encoding.marker_means: orange pills 'New' and 'Optional' tag the two inputs; parenthesised captions under card titles give the input-output pair or the contents
encoding.emphasis: three big tinted containers with 9 pt bold titles carry the system; everything else is 5-6 pt text on white cards; no single contribution is singled out since all three components are the contribution

lessons.what_to_learn: Give each system component its own tinted container and carry that tint onto the arrows that leave it; inside, white cards with a stock icon and a parenthesised input-output caption keep a dense system legible without step numbers. An offset stack of cards says 'many items' for a registry.
lessons.suits: Framework or benchmark-infrastructure papers with three or four named components, one input stage and a fan-out of artifacts.

evidence: JBF-FORGE is a multi-agent workflow that performs paper understanding, code synthesis, and fidelity verification.
JBF-LIB provides shared contracts and utilities, JBF-FORGE translates papers into runnable modules
Built on top, JBF-EVAL fixes datasets/loaders, execution protocols across victim models and decoding settings

summary: Jailbreak Foundry (JBF) turns published jailbreak-attack papers into executable modules and evaluates them under one unified harness, so attack success rates can be compared across papers and victim models. Figure 1 is a single system diagram. A new paper, with an optional reference repository, enters the blue JBF-FORGE container, whose Planner, Coder and Auditor cards produce a runnable module. A blue arrow registers it in the grey JBF-LIB container (contracts, LLM utilities, caching and logging, and a stacked-card registry). A grey arrow instantiates and runs it in the peach JBF-EVAL container (datasets, protocols, judge), which fans out to versioned results, comparable metrics and artifacts. Every card carries a flat stock icon, and each arrow takes the colour of the module it leaves.
summary_zh: Jailbreak Foundry 系统总览：新论文（可选参考仓库）经蓝色 FORGE 的规划、编码、审计智能体变成攻击模块，注册进灰色 LIB，再由桃色 EVAL 统一运行，输出版本化结果、指标和日志。
notes: Icon origin (stock, Flaticon-like family) is inferred from the uniform outlined style. The dashed grey loop is labelled Continuous Ingestion and Versioned Release; the paper text does not explain it, so only the figure's own words are recorded. Prior label 'panels=3' was not kept: the three tinted containers are stages of one connected drawing, not separate panels.
